article.title: Acusativo masculino inanimado = nominativo
article.chapter: Nominativo y cópula cero en presente — Именительный падеж и нулевая связка

claims.summary: For Russian masculine consonant-declension nouns, accusative singular inanimates match nominative while animates match genitive.
In Я знаю этот ресторан, ресторан is an inanimate accusative object whose form matches nominative; animacy differentiates the accusative from the nominative in the paired masculine animate example.
Cornell’s grammar provides Я знаю этот ресторан and Я знаю этого профессора to illustrate the inanimate/animate accusative contrast.
The described syncretism is limited to masculine consonant-declension nouns in singular and depends on animacy; it is not a universal ending rule.

locator.description: Cornell, Beginning Russian grammar, “Acc. Sg. and Plur. endings and animacy,” lines 0–12: lines 0–2 distinguish animate/inanimate and state singular masculine syncretism; lines 7–12 give Я знаю этого профессора and Я знаю этот ресторан in the same contrast.

links.notes: The article now uses the exact paired example attested on this page and limits the rule to the declension/number described there.
